prompt: A ticket app shows "2 seats left" and the theatre really has 5. Where is the defect most likely to be?

choices.text: In the phone's screen, which drew the number
choices.why: The screen draws what it was sent; it did not count anything.

choices.text: In the answer the server sent
choices.why: Right. The server counted and the app repeated its answer.

choices.text: In the network between the two
choices.why: A network delivers text or fails to; it does not change 5 into 2.

choices.text: In the test that found it
choices.why: The test only reported what both showed.

prompt: Which of these are reasons the section gives for testing at the API before testing the screen?

choices.text: A request answers in milliseconds
choices.why: Right: under a hundredth of a second here.

choices.text: It can send values the app never sends
choices.why: Right: seven seats, when the app stops at six.

choices.text: It makes the app's own tests unnecessary
choices.why: The section says the opposite: lessons 14 to 22 exist for what only the app can get wrong.

choices.text: No animation or sleeping phone makes it fail
choices.why: Right: when it fails, the answer was wrong.

prompt: Why does the course recommend installing the tools on your own system rather than in a virtual machine?

choices.text: Because Node, curl and jq cannot run inside a virtual machine at all
choices.why: Node runs in a virtual machine as it does anywhere else.

choices.text: Because the emulator would need nested virtualisation there
choices.why: Right. The second half runs on your own system anyway, so the first half may as well.

choices.text: Because the transcripts were recorded on a laptop
choices.why: They were recorded on Ubuntu 24.04, which a virtual machine runs as well.

choices.text: Because every hypervisor that runs Ubuntu is a paid product
choices.why: VirtualBox and UTM are free; cost is not the argument.

prompt: Why does the lesson install Node from nodejs.org instead of with apt-get?

choices.text: apt-get cannot install programs written in JavaScript
choices.why: apt installs programs in any language; Ubuntu has a nodejs package.

choices.text: nodejs.org is faster to download from
choices.why: Speed is not the reason given.

choices.text: Ubuntu's Node 18 is too old
choices.why: Right. The tools of lessons 6 and 15 need a newer one.

choices.text: The tarball includes boxoffice
choices.why: boxoffice is a file you save yourself in the next section.

prompt: The show sh-103 costs 6500 in price_cents. How many reais is one ticket?
You placed two orders, stopped boxoffice with Ctrl-C and started it again. What is the id of the next order you place?
hint: Where does boxoffice keep its orders?

choices.text: ord-1003, because the counter continues
choices.why: The counter lives in memory, and memory is gone after a restart.
Right. Everything lives in memory, so a restart puts boxoffice back as it began.

choices.text: ord-1002, because the first was cancelled
choices.why: Nothing was cancelled; a restart forgets every order.

choices.text: None: the restart refuses new orders until the old ones are deleted
choices.why: boxoffice has no old orders after a restart to delete.

prompt: Match each message to what it means.
hint: The last section shows each one.

pairs.right: nothing is listening on that port
another program already holds the port
the saved file stops before its end

prompt: What exit code did curl give when boxoffice was not running?
A classmate starts boxoffice, gets EADDRINUSE, and every request they send still answers normally. What is going on?

choices.text: The second boxoffice started anyway, on a random port
choices.why: It stopped at once; Node does not move to another port on its own.

choices.text: The requests are answered from curl's cache
choices.why: curl keeps no cache of answers between runs.

choices.text: An earlier boxoffice is still running and answers them
choices.why: Right. That one holds the port; the new one never started.

choices.text: EADDRINUSE is only a warning, and the server goes on running normally
choices.why: It is a fatal error: the process exits after printing it.

prompt: In `curl -v` output, what do the lines starting with `<` show?
hint: Arrows point the way the text travelled.

choices.text: What curl sent to the server
choices.why: Those are the `>` lines.

choices.text: What the server answered
choices.why: Right. The body follows with no mark.

choices.text: curl's notes about the connection
choices.why: Those start with `*`.

choices.text: Errors that stopped the request
choices.why: An error is reported on a line of its own; `<` is the response.

prompt: Put the parts of an HTTP response in the order they arrive.
A response has status 500 and a body that holds exactly the show you expected. What does a tester conclude?
hint: Which part is read first, and why?

choices.text: The request worked, since the data is right
choices.why: A client trusts the code first; this one says the server failed.

choices.text: A defect: the code says it failed
choices.why: Right. A right body under a 500 is not a right answer.

choices.text: The body is a cached copy and can be ignored
choices.why: Nothing in the response says cache; the code is the claim.

choices.text: Nothing until the request is sent ten more times
choices.why: The answer in front of you is already evidence.

remove what is at this address

prompt: Pressing Buy twice on a slow connection bought two tickets, while pressing Cancel twice cancelled one order once. Which property explains the difference?

choices.text: POST is safe and DELETE is not
choices.why: Neither is safe: both change the server.

choices.text: DELETE is answered faster than POST
choices.why: Speed would not stop a second request from acting.

choices.text: DELETE is idempotent, and POST is not idempotent
choices.why: Right. Repeating DELETE leaves the state as one did; repeating POST creates again.

choices.text: The app retries POST and never DELETE
choices.why: Both presses were the user's; the methods differ, not the app.

prompt: Why is boxoffice's answer to `curl -I` a defect?

choices.text: Servers must support HEAD, and boxoffice answers 405
choices.why: Right, and its own allow header says GET works, which HEAD mirrors.

choices.text: A HEAD response must carry the body too
choices.why: HEAD is exactly a GET without the body.

choices.text: 405 should have been 404
choices.why: The show exists, so 404 would be a second defect.

choices.text: curl -I sends a DELETE, which should be allowed
choices.why: -I sends HEAD; -X DELETE is the other request.

prompt: Match each order request to the code boxoffice answered.

pairs.left: the order sent as a form

prompt: A server answers 503 to a request whose JSON is malformed. What should the bug report say?
hint: Who does each class blame, and what does it tell the client to do?

choices.text: Nothing: any error code is acceptable for a bad request
choices.why: The class is a claim about who failed; a client acts on it.

choices.text: It should be 400, since the fault is wholly the client's
choices.why: Right. The request is wrong; sending it again will fail again.

choices.text: It should be 422, which is the code for every malformed body sent
choices.why: 422 is for valid JSON that breaks a rule; malformed JSON is 400.

choices.text: It should be 200 with an error message in the body
choices.why: That hides the failure from every client that reads the code first.

prompt: A request that created something new is answered with status ___, and the location header says where it lives.
You want to check that selling a seat changes the etag of sh-101. Which test does that?
hint: The fingerprint has to be compared before and after the change.

choices.text: Read sh-101 twice in a row and check that both etags it returns are equal
choices.why: That checks the etag is stable, not that it changes when the show does.

choices.text: Note its etag, buy a seat, send the old etag in if-none-match, expect 200
choices.why: Right. A 304 there would be a server saying a stale copy is current.

choices.text: Buy a seat and expect the order's own response to carry an etag header too
choices.why: The order's response is about the order, not the show.

choices.text: Send if-none-match with a made-up value and expect 304
choices.why: A value the server never issued should never match.
